title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s reply to the 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards outlines its plans to strengthen transparency, accountability, and safety in AI use. It commits to developing clearer regulations, fostering public trust, and ensuring AI systems are fair, robust, and aligned with societal values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining its plan to regulate how artificial intelligence can be used in educational qualifications, ensuring fairness, reliability, and transparency in exams and assessments. The policy is a response to a request from key government officials to create guidelines that protect students, maintain academic integrity, and promote responsible AI use in the qualifications sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report investigates how using copyrighted works to train AI models affects creators, consumers, and the wider economy. It provides an impact assessment and offers policy recommendations to balance intellectual property rights with AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has replied to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on artificial intelligence, acknowledging the urgent need for stronger safeguards and clearer regulations. It outlines plans to boost investment in AI research, improve public trust, and enforce stricter oversight to ensure technology benefits society while mitigating risks.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the scope and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing the role of artificial intelligence in public standards, including its purpose, structure, and decision‑making processes. It also includes frequently asked questions that clarify the committee’s roles, procedures, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into how artificial intelligence should be governed. In its submission, the CSPL outlines concerns and offers recommendations on regulating and monitoring AI.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how artificial intelligence will change the rules for medical products and the steps needed to incorporate the AI White Paper’s guidelines. It offers a framework for regulators and industry to adapt safety, transparency, and accountability measures to AI‑driven medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence AI Strategy aims to make our organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI user in defence for a country of our size. It outlines how we will develop, adopt, and responsibly deploy AI technologies to strengthen our defence capabilities and maintain international leadership.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to take advantage of artificial intelligence. It also describes how the government will manage and reduce the risks that come with using AI in transport.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyright works are used in AI development under the Data (Use and Access) Act. It assesses progress, challenges, and the balance between innovation and rights protection.
